title: Trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1) · metastatic

agents.name: Trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1)
agents.type: HER2-directed antibody with a chemotherapy payload
agents.mechanism: HER2 targeting carries DM1 into cancer cells.
agents.explanation: The antibody attaches to HER2. After the complex enters a cell, its DM1 payload disrupts structures needed for cell division. This is a single linked medicine, with its own dosing and safety rules.
agents.watch: Report bleeding, numbness, jaundice, new cough or breathlessness. Keep blood and heart checks.

context_label: Previously treated HER2-positive unresectable locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer
purpose: T-DM1 links HER2 targeting to a chemotherapy payload to help control previously treated advanced breast cancer. Prior trastuzumab and a taxane, plus the full NCCP prior-treatment or early-relapse criteria, must be checked.
schedule_summary: T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV every 21 days, adjusted if required, until progression or unacceptable toxicity. This metastatic course has no fixed 14-cycle endpoint; the postoperative early-breast regimen is a different card.

phases_note: Early and metastatic pathways have different aims and endpoints. The team confirms the applicable plan.
timeline_note: Treatment days show the planned schedule. Symptom bands are broad possibilities, not measured risk curves or guaranteed safe days.
safety_note: New breathlessness, chest pain, collapse, severe allergic symptoms or sudden serious illness need urgent assessment on any day.
teachback: What is the purpose of your treatment? Which heart or blood test is due next, and which team arranges and reviews it?
consent_support: Discuss expected benefit, alternatives, route, duration, cardiac monitoring, pregnancy / contraception, urgent contacts and individual treatment risks. Add any companion drug using its own regimen information.
urgent_extra: Call promptly for unusual bleeding, yellow eyes / skin, worsening numbness or new cough / breathlessness.

support.title: Support for this medicine
support.text: T-DM1 has low emetogenic risk; review the low-risk antiemetic draft and individual contraindications.

support.title: Blood and heart appointments
support.text: FBC, renal and liver profile before every cycle. Echo / MUGA every 12 weeks; around C5 for uninterrupted 21-day cycles.

support.title: Local treatment and endocrine therapy
support.text: Surgery and radiotherapy are coordinated by the MDT. When endocrine therapy is indicated, it has its own schedule and bone-health plan.

support.title: Pregnancy / contraception
support.text: Discuss pregnancy, fertility and contraception before treatment. Report pregnancy promptly; do not breastfeed during treatment or for 7 months afterwards. The team confirms the medicine-specific contraception duration.

questions.q: How long will I receive treatment?
questions.a: T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV every 21 days, adjusted if required, until progression or unacceptable toxicity. This metastatic course has no fixed 14-cycle endpoint; the postoperative early-breast regimen is a different card.
Echo / MUGA every 12 weeks; around C5 for uninterrupted 21-day cycles. Existing HER2 exposure and delays affect cycle numbering; the team should give the actual due window.
Radiotherapy is used for a defined site or symptom when indicated. The oncology and radiation teams agree whether this medicine continues or pauses; do not infer a concurrent schedule from this card.

questions.q: Does a tumour marker replace a scan?
questions.a: No. In metastatic disease it may add information to symptoms and imaging. It should not alone determine treatment changes. In symptom-free early disease it is not routine recurrence screening.

evidence.title: EMILIA · original analysis (2012)
evidence.intro: Evidence belongs to a specified population and treatment setting.
evidence.population: 991 patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer previously treated with trastuzumab and a taxane.
evidence.interpretation: T-DM1 improved progression-free and overall survival versus lapatinib plus capecitabine in this historical trial. It does not establish today’s preferred sequence among all HER2 medicines. Group medians do not predict an individual survival time.

chapters.title: Your treatment aim
chapters.intro: T-DM1 links HER2 targeting to a chemotherapy payload to help control previously treated advanced breast cancer. Prior trastuzumab and a taxane, plus the full NCCP prior-treatment or early-relapse criteria, must be checked.

items.title: Setting and duration
items.text: T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV every 21 days, adjusted if required, until progression or unacceptable toxicity. This metastatic course has no fixed 14-cycle endpoint; the postoperative early-breast regimen is a different card.

items.title: Medicine identity
items.text: T-DM1 is a single antibody–drug conjugate. It is not interchangeable with trastuzumab alone or trastuzumab deruxtecan.

chapters.title: Before treatment and between visits
chapters.intro: The team should arrange and review the tests.

items.title: Blood checks
items.text: FBC, renal and liver profile before every cycle

items.title: Cardiac checks
items.text: Echo / MUGA every 12 weeks; around C5 for uninterrupted 21-day cycles. Baseline cardiac assessment and LVEF are required. ECG is guided by the cardiac / clinical assessment; NCCP does not prescribe a separate fixed-cycle ECG timetable for T-DM1.

items.title: After stopping
items.text: Agree follow-up of cardiac, liver, platelet and nerve effects at any treatment change; no universal post-T-DM1 scan calendar is assigned here.

chapters.title: The wider pathway
chapters.intro: Coordinate cancer medicines with local treatment and follow-up.

items.title: Scans and markers
items.text: Response imaging commonly every 2–4 months, adapted to sites, disease course and treatment. A new symptom can need earlier imaging. Tumour markers may supplement assessment, never determine a treatment change alone.

items.title: Radiotherapy relationship
items.text: Radiotherapy is used for a defined site or symptom when indicated. The oncology and radiation teams agree whether this medicine continues or pauses; do not infer a concurrent schedule from this card.

items.title: Bone health
items.text: If an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression is planned, assess fracture risk and DEXA need. Repeat timing depends on results and bone treatment; this is not an automatic HER2-therapy scan.

chronology_notes.title: No date entry needed
chronology_notes.text: This is an orientation map; it does not calculate a personal appointment calendar.

chronology_notes.title: Delayed treatment
chronology_notes.text: Blood tests and echoes follow clinical due windows. A postponed dose does not automatically postpone monitoring.

chronology_notes.title: Companion medicines
chronology_notes.text: If another cancer medicine is prescribed, its side effects, tests and supportive medicines need its own plan.

logistics.title: Your practical treatment plan
logistics.intro: T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV every 21 days, adjusted if required, until progression or unacceptable toxicity. This metastatic course has no fixed 14-cycle endpoint; the postoperative early-breast regimen is a different card.

steps.title: Before your visit
steps.text: Confirm the dose, symptoms, required blood results and echo due window.

steps.title: Access and administration
steps.text: A cannula, PICC or implanted port may be used according to the treatment plan. A port insertion is a separate procedure.

steps.title: Treatment and observation
steps.text: First infusion over 90 minutes, then observe for at least 90 minutes. Later infusions may take 30 minutes if tolerated, with at least 30 minutes observation.

steps.title: After the visit
steps.text: Contact the unit to rearrange a missed dose; the next schedule preserves a 3-week interval. This medicine does not routinely require a take-home pump.

details.title: Port insertion and removal
details.text: The line team explains placement, dressing care and when normal activities can resume. A port is accessed with a special needle during treatment. Removal of the implanted device is a separate planned procedure when no longer needed; do not remove or adjust it yourself.

details.title: PICC care and urgent line symptoms
details.text: A PICC usually needs regular dressing and flushing appointments even between treatments. Fever, redness, swelling, pain, leakage or damage requires prompt advice. Your hospital supplies the exact care instructions.

details.title: Visit length
details.text: First infusion over 90 minutes, then observe for at least 90 minutes. Later infusions may take 30 minutes if tolerated, with at least 30 minutes observation.

details.title: Missed or delayed visit
details.text: Contact the unit to rearrange a missed dose; the next schedule preserves a 3-week interval.

anatomy: New cough or breathlessness: seek prompt assessment.
Keep echo checks. Report swelling, chest symptoms, fainting or rapid weight gain.
Keep liver blood tests. Report yellow eyes / skin, dark urine or significant abdominal symptoms.
Report unexplained bruising or bleeding; heavy or persistent bleeding needs urgent help.
Report numbness or tingling, especially if it affects walking or hand use.

monitoring_schedule.title: When your checks happen
monitoring_schedule.note: Cycle examples assume no delays and count from the first dose of this schedule. If switching route or continuing previous HER2 treatment, preserve the existing echo due date. Tests are scheduled by elapsed time and clinical need; the team owns booking and result review. NCCP remains 12-weekly during treatment, including maintenance; a longer interval needs an explicit individual specialist plan.
